ask.hint: For example: which machines still expose RDP, which NAS has findings, which devices are new.

meter.title: Token meter
meter.description: Tokens used with your provider. Vedette charges nothing; you pay the provider directly.

runs.caption: Log of AI calls
runs.filter: Filter by task, target or model

status.failed: Failed: not sent or not answered

settings.title: AI assistant
settings.statusOn: AI profiles are set up. Each task uses the profile you assign to it below.
settings.statusOff: No usable AI profile yet. The Ask AI buttons stay off until you add one.

flow.title: What data leaves this box
flow.remote: Data for tasks assigned to cloud profiles goes to {{hosts}} using your key. It is covered by your own agreement with that provider.
flow.rules: Data does not pass through any Vedette server and keys never leave this box. With no profile saved, nothing is sent. Email addresses and phone numbers are masked before sending unless you turn that hook off.
flow.abroad: If a cloud provider hosts its servers outside Vietnam and the data sent contains personal data (user names or emails in logs), this may count as a cross-border transfer of personal data under Vietnam's Law on Personal Data Protection No. 91/2025/QH15 (Article 20). Keep personal data masking on below, use a profile inside your network for internal data, and see the assessment on the Reports page.
flow.noneRemote: No cloud profile is set up, so nothing leaves your network. Profiles inside your network keep data on it.

tier.title: Token level
tier.intro: The level decides how much one log digest sends and whether the AI may check points with read-only tools. Log digests, explanations, CVE news and report comments run only when someone clicks. Response plans, once you give them a profile, run by themselves (every 5 minutes, at most 20 calls a day); the level does not change them. Past the daily cap Vedette lowers the level itself and records it.

min.name: Minimum
min.sends: Short log digests: at most 5 new kinds of line, 5 spikes and 5 bad connections.

med.name: Medium
med.sends: Full log digests: up to 20 new kinds of line, 20 spikes and 20 bad connections.

max.name: Maximum
max.sends: Full log digests, and the AI may check points with read-only tools (Log investigation): what the logs counted for an address, devices, threat feeds and the exploited list.

tier.estimate: Suggested daily cap at this level: {{n}} tokens.
tier.estimateMax: Depends on how many tool calls the AI makes; you set the cap below.

settings.cap: Daily token cap for all profiles together
settings.capHint: From 1,000 to 5,000,000. The medium level default is 60,000. Each profile also has its own cap.
settings.redactHint: This is the Block personal data hook: it masks email addresses and phone numbers, and stops a call whose text holds an ID number, before anything is sent. It also masks device secrets that come with their marker in configurations, log lines and tool results (passwords, password hashes, SNMP communities, keys). A password or token in free text is not caught; add a hook for those.

err.cap: The cap must be a whole number from 1,000 to 5,000,000.

retention.title: Activity log retention
retention.intro: How long the AI activity log is kept. Entries are never edited or deleted before then.
retention.label: Keep for (days)
retention.err: Enter a whole number of days, at least 90.

cve.explainDesc: The AI reads the CVE data and your devices, then says whether you are affected and how to fix it. The result is saved, so asking again costs no tokens.
cve.explainEmpty: Click Explain and the AI explains it in plain English.
cve.newsDesc: The box fetches the vendor advisory, GitHub PoC search results and a few security news feeds, then asks the AI to summarise. The AI does not browse the web itself.
cve.newsEmpty: Click to have the box fetch the sources and summarise.

affected.unknown: You may be affected, check the version

cve.newsMeta: Summarised {{time}}. Fetched text is marked as data, stripped of control characters and checked by your hooks before it reaches the AI.

logs.title: AI log digest
logs.description: The AI reads aggregated logs and says what to look at first. Logs are untrusted data: the AI only summarises and does nothing on your behalf.
logs.none: No summary has been made at this level yet. Press Regenerate now.
logs.cite: Kinds of log line and their counts on this box, never the lines
logs.noItems: Nothing in the current log data needs a look.
logs.suggested_one: The AI suggested 1 memory about this network. Nothing is remembered until an administrator accepts it.
logs.suggested_other: The AI suggested {{count}} memories about this network. Nothing is remembered until an administrator accepts them.
logs.suggestedLink: Review in Settings, AI assistant, Memory

profiles.title: AI profiles
profiles.description: A profile is one AI you can use: provider, model, key and where it runs. Add several, for example a fast cheap model and a strong one, or a model on your own network.
profiles.caption: AI profiles
profiles.emptyBody: Add one to turn on explanations, log digests and asking your data. Anthropic, OpenAI and Gemini keys, a local Ollama or vLLM server, or any compatible service all work.
profiles.testDetail: {{name}} replied in {{ms}} ms. The test used {{input}} tokens in, {{output}} tokens out.
profiles.capNoTools: The model cannot call tools; investigation tasks will not work well with it.
profiles.dialogBody: The key is stored encrypted on this box. Only its last 4 characters are shown afterwards.
profiles.removeBody: No task uses this profile. Its run history stays in the log.
profiles.removeBodyUsed: It is assigned to: {{jobs}}. A task that loses its primary profile moves up its fallback; otherwise it stops until you assign another.

f.name: Profile name
f.nameHint: Shown in the run log and on every AI answer, for example Claude Sonnet.
f.styleHint: Which API the server speaks. Most self-hosted servers use OpenAI Chat Completions.
f.baseUrlCloud: Must be https://. Keep the default if you use the provider directly.
f.baseUrlInternal: A server on your own network may use http://. Ollama answers on http://server-IP:11434/v1 (vLLM on port 8000); start Ollama with OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0 so the box can reach it. Ollama on the machine that runs Vedette: http://localhost:11434/v1 with a package install; with a container install localhost is the container itself, so use http://host.containers.internal:11434/v1 (Podman), http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1 (Docker) or the machine's LAN IP.
f.modelHint: A small model suits batch jobs such as log digests; a stronger one suits explanations. Model names change over time: if the connection test says the model does not exist, copy the name from the provider's model page.
f.keySaved: A key ending in {{last4}} is stored. Leave empty to keep it; enter a new key to replace it.
f.keyOptional: A server inside your network may not need a key.
f.keyHint: Encrypted on this box; only the last 4 characters are shown after saving.
f.location_internal: On your own network or machine (Ollama, vLLM). Internal means the address is inside your network; data sent to it may leave if it forwards to a cloud provider.
f.location_cloud: A provider's cloud service. Data sent to it leaves your network.
f.cloudOnly: Anthropic, OpenAI and Gemini run in the cloud. Choose OpenAI-compatible or Custom for a server on your own network.
f.cap: Daily token cap for this profile
f.capHint: From 1,000 to 5,000,000. When the cap is reached, tasks move to their fallback profile.
f.ack: I understand the data for tasks assigned to this profile will be sent to {{host}}.

err.name: Enter a profile name.
err.duplicate: Another profile already has this name.
err.style: Pick the API style the server speaks.
err.url: The address is not valid. Enter it in full, for example https://api.anthropic.com.
err.https: The address must start with https://. Only a server inside your own network may use http://.
err.model: Enter a model name, for example claude-haiku-5-5.
err.keyRequired: Enter the provider's API key. It stays on this box and is encrypted.
err.keyMoved: Changing the address needs the API key entered again.
err.keyShape: The key is too short or contains spaces. Copy the whole key again from the provider's console.
err.cap: The cap must be a whole number from 1,000 to 5,000,000.

assign.title: Job routing
assign.description: Each AI task uses a primary profile and, optionally, a fallback. Vedette switches to the fallback when the primary fails, times out or reaches its daily cap, and records which profile answered.
assign.rule: Logs and device data go only to profiles inside your network
assign.ruleBody: On: tasks that send your logs, devices or findings (summaries, investigation, asking your data, explanations, reports) can only use profiles that run inside your network, so that data never leaves it. Tasks on public data (CVE news, translating vendor advisories) may still use cloud profiles. Off: any profile can be used for any task.
assign.suggested: Suggestion applied below. Review it, then save.
assign.suggestedSame: Your saved routing already matches the suggestion. Nothing to save.
assign.cleared: {{count}} cloud assignment(s) were cleared because the rule allows only internal profiles for that data. Save to apply.
assign.noProfilesBody: Add an AI profile above; a profile that needs a key is not usable until the key is saved.
assign.caption: AI job routing
assign.optCloud: cloud, not allowed for internal data
assign.fallbackNote: The suggestion puts a fast model on batch tasks such as log digests, news and translation, and a strong model on tasks that need reasoning such as explanations and asking your data. Between two profiles that fit equally, a task with internal data gets the one inside your network. To keep internal data on your network whatever the model, turn on the rule above.

rules.builtinBody: Sent with every AI call. They keep the AI inside its job and cannot be changed or turned off.
rules.customBody: Extra instructions added to AI calls, for example how to name devices or your change window.
rules.emptyBody: Add a rule to tell the AI something it should always follow in this company.
rules.dialogBody: The rule is added to the instructions of every chosen AI job.
rules.textHint: One clear instruction, for example: Always name devices by hostname and IP address.
rules.errText: Write the rule in at least 3 characters.

memory.suggestHint: When on, the AI can propose things it noticed about this network. Nothing is remembered until you accept it.
memory.title: What the AI remembers
memory.body: Facts about this network the AI keeps between questions. You can edit, turn off or delete any of them.
memory.emptyBody: Add a fact about your network, for example how a device is exposed, so the AI does not have to guess.
memory.dialogBody: The AI reads enabled memories before it answers questions about your network.
memory.textHint: A fact, for example: NAS-PHOTOS is reachable from the Internet through FortiGate virtual IP NAS-PHOTO-443.
memory.errText: Write the memory in at least 3 characters.

skills.title: Skills
skills.body: The ready-made jobs the AI can do. Turn a skill off and its job stops running.
skills.batch: Runs in batches during inventory, not from a button.

knowledge.indexBody: The index is built on this box with full-text search. Building it sends no document text to any AI provider. A profile is still required for now.
knowledge.indexHint: Building the index sends nothing out. While the privacy rule is on, a cloud profile cannot be chosen.
knowledge.cloudWarn: This is a cloud profile. Building the index sends nothing to {{host}}.
knowledge.internalNote: This profile runs inside your network, so document text stays here.
knowledge.title: Documents
knowledge.body: Network diagrams, policies and runbooks the AI can look things up in. PDF, MD, TXT or DOCX, up to 10 MB each.
knowledge.needIndex: Choose an AI profile for the index first.
knowledge.errType: {{name}} cannot be added. Use a PDF, MD, TXT or DOCX file.
knowledge.errRead: {{name}} could not be read. Pick the file again.
knowledge.emptyBody: Upload a network diagram or your security policy and the AI can use it when it explains findings.
knowledge.jobsBody: Only the chosen jobs can read this document.
knowledge.jobsLegend: Jobs that may use this document
knowledge.deleteBody: The document and its index are removed from this box. This cannot be undone.

hooks.body: Hooks are checks that run before and after every AI call.
hooks.lockedWhy: A tool that changes something can only run through an action a person approves. This hook cannot be turned off.
hooks.customBody: Look for words or a pattern in what is sent to the AI, in its answer, or in a tool call, then block it, mask it or hold it for approval.
hooks.emptyBody: Add a hook to stop something specific, for example a project code name leaving your network.
hooks.tryBody: Type a sample text and see what the hooks that are on would do with it.
hooks.sampleHint: For example: email me at an.nguyen@example.com
hooks.dialogBody: A hook runs on every AI call at the stage you choose.
hooks.errPattern: Enter the words or the pattern to look for.
hooks.errMessage: Write the message people will see.

f.name: Name
f.actionHint_block: The text is not sent or the answer is not shown.
f.actionHint_mask: The matching part is replaced with [masked].
f.actionHint_approve: The call waits until a person approves it.
f.patternHint_keywords: Separate words with commas, for example: project falcon, salary
f.messageHint: Say why it acted and what to do next.

hooks.deleteBody: The hook stops checking AI calls straight away.

activity.title: Activity log
activity.description: Everything the AI did on this box: who or what started it, the checks that acted, the tools it used, and hashes of what was sent and answered. The content itself is not stored.
activity.caption: AI activity log
activity.empty: No AI activity matches these filters.
activity.broken: Chain broken at entry {{n}}: this entry or an earlier one was changed after it was written.
activity.readOnly: Entries cannot be edited or deleted. They are kept for {{days}} days; change this in Settings, AI assistant.

detail.title: {{job}}
detail.note: hash = SHA-256 of the previous hash plus the entry's canonical JSON (sorted keys, without hash). Download the logs in Settings, Data to verify offline.
